headline: Newcastle lose again: still the favourites at Palace?
summary: Newcastle arrive at Selhurst Park after a 0-1 home defeat by Aston Villa on Friday — their second straight league loss. Palace's week was worse: a 0-5 defeat at Brighton, and BBC Sport reports Pierre Sage is fighting to keep his job. Palace have conceded 9 goals in their last 5 games, while Newcastle still created 1.84 expected goals at Coventry. That contrast explains the prices: Newcastle's win chance has risen from 37.5% to 40.8%, and the market rates them about a quarter of a goal stronger. Over 3 goals is a 48.3% chance.
read: Two managers under pressure meet at Selhurst Park: Palace on the back of a 0-5 defeat at Brighton, Newcastle after two straight losses of their own. The market still makes Newcastle the favourites and expects an open game of about three goals.

facts.fact: Crystal Palace lost 5-0 at rivals Brighton on Sunday, conceding three goals inside the first 10 minutes.
facts.meaning: Palace come into a home game against a direct rival off a five-goal derby defeat, with the manager's position in the news.

facts.fact: Palace are 14th with 7 points from 7 games, and BBC Sport reports manager Pierre Sage is fighting to keep his job but will be given more time.
facts.meaning: Sage is expected to be in charge on Sunday, per The Athletic, so this home game is his immediate chance to answer the pressure.

facts.fact: Newcastle lost 0-1 at home to Aston Villa on Friday, their second straight league defeat after a 1-4 loss at Coventry.
facts.meaning: Newcastle arrive with a crisis of their own — this is not a confident side coming to Selhurst Park.

facts.fact: Newcastle's chance of winning has risen from 37.5% to 40.8% in recent days.
facts.meaning: Newcastle are the clear favourites for a match away from home, with Palace the outsiders on their own ground.

facts.fact: The Athletic reports pressure on Newcastle manager Matthias Jaissle over his tactics amid the club's collapsing form, with Newcastle having scored only 5 goals in their last five games.
facts.meaning: Both dugouts are under scrutiny on Sunday, and Newcastle's problem is scoring as much as results.

facts.fact: The goal line is set at 3.0, with over priced at 48.3% — effectively a coin flip on three goals or more.
facts.meaning: A high total for a Premier League game: the market expects an open, high-scoring match rather than a tight one.

facts.fact: Palace have conceded 9 goals in their last five games, and The Athletic reports they lost centre-backs Marc Guehi and Maxence Lacroix in 2026, replacing them with loanees and youngsters.
facts.meaning: A rebuilt, inexperienced back line is the football reason Palace are underdogs at home.

facts.fact: The handicap fair line has moved from 0.04 to 0.17, with Palace now receiving +0.25 on the main line.
facts.meaning: The market rates Newcastle roughly a quarter of a goal the better side, even away from Selhurst Park.

sources.fact: BBC Sport reports that Crystal Palace boss Pierre Sage faces a fight to keep his job but will be given more time.
Crystal Palace lost 5-0 at rivals Brighton, conceding three goals in the first 10 minutes, including a Diego Gomez strike from the halfway line.
The Athletic reports that Palace do not intend to make an immediate managerial change and Sage is expected to take charge of Sunday's home match against Newcastle.
The Athletic reports that Palace lost centre-halves Marc Guehi and Maxence Lacroix in 2026 and replaced them with loanees and youngsters, with an obvious drop-off in quality.
Left-back Tyrick Mitchell urged struggling Palace to get "back to basics" ahead of their Europa League trip to Besiktas, as they look to bounce back from the 5-0 defeat to Brighton.
The Standard reports Sage knows results need to change, with Palace facing potentially critical games against Besiktas and Newcastle this week.
The Athletic reports on pressure on Newcastle manager Matthias Jaissle amid the club's collapsing form and questions over his tactics.
Matthias Jaissle has dropped hints on the fitness of key men Dan Burn and William Osula ahead of Sunday's trip to Crystal Palace.
